text:
𝗜𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝗜 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂, 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗔𝗜.

This is a bit of my pain right now, because I'm replacing people who don't automate their work with people who do. And it's not that I enjoy it — I genuinely don't. These are real people. But keeping both the AI and the person doing the same job just doesn't make sense anymore.

And the hard part is — nothing is actually stopping people from learning this, and that's what gets to me.

So here's my idea: 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗔𝗜, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁. We only do maybe 10% of the work we actually could be doing. When you push that 10% to AI, you go find the next thing, try to implement it through AI, find something else, and implement again. And at some point, 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗽 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗷𝗼𝗯: 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝘁, 𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗶𝘁, 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗔𝗜. Nothing in our world replaces that. 🔄

A simple example. We have a PM who automated turning meeting recordings into Jira updates. Used to do it all by hand — listening back, changing statuses, writing comments. Then AI started doing it, and a client saw it and wanted the same for their team.

He didn't lose his job — 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗶𝗺 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲, 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗵𝗶𝗺. Because he's not the person who updates Jira anymore, he's the person who knows what to automate and how to make it actually work, with his hands being just the UI on top of the system. 💡

Everyone is hiring people who do this right now, and letting go of people who don't. Use it.
